CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the response to the current treatment regimen for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to evaluate any new developments since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the treatment plan. He states that while his anxiety levels have remained stable, he continues to experience episodes of irritability, particularly in high-pressure situations at work. Mr. Smith has been compliant with his sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily but expresses dissatisfaction with the lack of substantial improvement in his mood and concentration.
His tension-type headaches have remained stable, occurring about once a week, with an intensity rating of 3 out of 10. He reports that the topiramate at 150 mg daily continues to be effective, and he has maintained his ibuprofen usage to once weekly, mindful of the gastrointestinal side effects he previously experienced.
Sleep quality has fluctuated; Mr. Smith reports averages of 6 to 8 hours of sleep per night but notes increased difficulty falling asleep on nights with heightened anxiety. He continues to take trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime, which he finds somewhat effective, though he still experiences residual drowsiness in the mornings. He has adhered to discontinuing gabapentin, which he felt was too sedating.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Smith reports persistent fatigue, particularly in the afternoons, which he describes as debilitating. He has made efforts to incorporate physical activity and mindfulness practices into his routine but finds that his energy levels remain insufficient for daily tasks. He expresses concern about the impact of fatigue on his productivity and overall quality of life.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (discontinued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in regular physical activity, participating in lunchtime walks and weekend hikes. He reports adherence to a balanced diet and has successfully reduced his caffeine intake. He remains committed to mindfulness techniques, including meditation and yoga, which he finds beneficial in managing anxiety symptoms. His journaling practice persists, aiding in self-reflection and mood tracking.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; mild irritability persists; sleep quality variable; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears fatigued; mood appears anxious but engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with mild distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to address irritability and concentration difficulties. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime; reassess efficacy and side effects in one month. Consider adding melatonin 3 mg if sleep onset continues to be problematic. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued lifestyle modifications and consider referral to a sleep specialist for evaluation of potential underlying conditions such as sleep apnea or thyroid dysfunction.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-02-23 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
